title: Unit – 2 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2 | Binary Arithmetic – Multiplication and Division
sections: Section A – Match the Following (Answers)
1. Binary Multiplication → B. Use 0/1 multiplication and shifting
2. Binary Division → A. Repeated subtraction and shifting
3. Multiplying by 0 → C. Always gives 0
4. Multiplying by 1 → D. Gives the same number
5. Shift Left → E. Equivalent to multiplying by 2
Section B – Fill in the Blanks
Binary multiplication uses only two operations: AND and SHIFT LEFT.
Division in binary uses repeated SUBTRACTION with right shifts.
Shifting left by one bit is equal to MULTIPLYING by 2.
Shifting right by one bit is equal to DIVIDING by 2.
If divisor is greater than the dividend, the quotient is 0 and the remainder is the DIVIDEND.

Section D – Activity Task (Binary Division)

(a) 10110 ÷ 101: 101 goes into 1011 once (quotient bit 1), remainder 0110 brings down; 101 > 011 → quotient bit 0; final: Quotient = 100, Remainder = 10. Check: 10110₂ = 22, 101₂ = 5 → 22 = 5×4 + 2, so Quotient = 100 (4), Remainder = 010 (2).

(b) 11001 ÷ 11: 11 into 110 twice (11), 11001 = 25, 11₂ = 3 → 25 = 3×8 + 1, so Quotient = 1000 (8), Remainder = 1. Long division: 11 into 110 → 1 (rem 0), bring 0 → 00 < 11 → 0, bring 1 → 001 < 11 → 0, final remainder 1 → Quotient = 1000, Remainder = 001.
Section E – True or False
Binary multiplication uses only 0, 1 and shifting. — TRUE
Division by shifting right is exact for any binary number. — FALSE (exact only when no 1-bits are shifted out, e.g. even numbers)
In binary multiplication, multiplying by 1 leaves the number unchanged. — TRUE
In binary division, if the divisor is bigger than the partial dividend, a 0 is placed in the quotient. — TRUE
Shifting left by two positions multiplies the number by 4. — TRUE
